methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Report: Data centers dominate Virginia’s economic development incentives
signals.signal_reading: Data center tax incentives consuming 60% of Virginia's economic development spending signals a policy preference for capital-intensive infrastructure over human capability building, widening the gap between capital-rich metros and regions needing workforce investment.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: AI Ready Roanoke represents distributed peer-network capacity building outside traditional tech hubs, signaling potential for grassroots AI fluency if evaluation translates into sustained community-driven adoption rather than vendor-dependent deployment.

signals.title: Virginia Tech outlines philosophy for AI adoption - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's institutional AI philosophy could deepen technical excellence in the New River Valley cluster while creating a knowledge transfer challenge—whether deep capability radiates outward or concentrates around the university ecosystem determines distribution.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: Governor's cybersecurity AI directive signals shallow, platform-mediated adoption—state agencies consuming vendor AI tools for defense creates broad surface-level exposure without building indigenous technical depth or distributed human capability.

signals.title: Sociologist: You want to see the next iteration of the company town? Come to Virginia.
signals.signal_reading: The company-town critique of data centers in Appalachian Virginia reveals extractive infrastructure patterns—massive capital investment concentrating power and resources while bypassing local capability development, echoing historical coal exploitation dynamics.
